chunks: You will notice that those whose hearts are afflicted with sickness (of doubt) only hasten to join them and say: 'We fear lest misfortune should surround us.' It may well be that God may soon send (you) success, or other command of His. Then will they be repentant of what they had concealed in their hearts.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'da'irah' in the context of the hypocrites in Surah Al-Ma'idah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological instability of the hypocrites, whose 'disease' is not merely physical but a spiritual malaise of insincerity that drives their opportunistic haste. Their fear of the 'da'irah' (circular turn of fate) reflects a transactional view of faith, where they align with Muslims only to avoid loss, anticipating that divine victory will expose their hidden duplicity. This underscores the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity), contrasting the hypocrites' external conformity with the genuine conviction of the faithful.
